title: Investigation runway and visibility radar
summary: Practical working doc for constructing a lightweight investigation runway: a compact set of signals, trace anchors, and dashboard patterns (the 'visibility radar') that let oncall and engineers triage inference incidents quickly while controlling telemetry cost.
content:
Context:
- Problem: when inference regressions or tenant-impact incidents happen we take too long to narrow scope (model vs infra vs routing). Full trace capture is expensive; we need a minimal, high-signal surface that accelerates hypothesis elimination.

Goal:
- Define a compact investigation runway (ordered signals to check) plus a visibility radar dashboard that highlights which subsystems to probe first.
- Keep telemetry cost predictable with adaptive sampling and per-incident trace escalation.

Audience:
- Oncall engineers, SREs, serving-runtime, and solutions engineers doing customer-facing RCA.

Principles (short):
- Order-of-elimination: surface cheap, high-precision signals first (cache-hit, batch sizes, queue length) before pulling traces.
- Severity-weighted sampling: capture more detail for high-severity/large-cost incidents.
- Tenant-context: always surface tenant_id/session_id/model_variant early.
- Cost guardrails: cap full-trace ingestion budget per hour and per-tenant.

Visibility radar (dashboard sketch):
- Ring A (fast checks, < 10s to query):
  * Real-time qps, p50/p95/p99 token-latency (per-route + per-tenant top-10)
  * KV cache hit rate and prefix-lookup latency
  * Batch size distribution (histogram), queue_time_ms percentiles
  * Fallback-rate (automatic model variant fallbacks)
  * Model-selection-latency (time to pick variant + compile cost if any)
- Ring B (requires lightweight traces / slightly heavier queries):
  * Request-path mix (chat vs completion vs embeddings) + per-path error breakdowns
  * Recent changes in per-tenant token-economics (tokens per request, avg seq_len)
  * Memory pressure alerts on GPU hosts (cache eviction spikes)
- Ring C (trace-first, heavier but targeted):
  * Sampled traces anchored on request_id/session_id/model_variant/tenant_id
  * KV-cache miss trace with prior-key context (to diagnose prefix mismatch)
  * Batching anomalies: traces that show long wait-for-batch durations

Metric definitions (compact):
- inference.request.count: count of inference requests (tagged: route, model_variant, tenant_id, region)
- inference.tokens.generated: token output count (same tags)
- inference.latency.token_ms.p50/p95/p99: per-token generation latency percentiles (include generation vs total request split)
- serving.queue_time.ms.p95: time waiting in scheduling queue before execution start
- serving.batch.size.p50/p95: observed batch size distribution for GPU workers
- kvcache.hit.rate: ratio (hits / lookups) computed per prefix window (5m) and per-tenant
- fallback.rate: percent of requests routed to fallback variant or lower-tier capacity
- model-selection.latency.ms: time taken to resolve model variant and quantization profile
- request.e2e.errors: count of user-visible errors (HTTP 5xx, tokenization failures)

Trace anchors and minimum span set:
- root span: request_id, tenant_id, route, model_variant, seq_length, sdk_version
- queue span: queue_id, queue_time_ms, host_shard
- batch span: batch_id, batch_size, batch_wait_ms, batch_exec_ms
- model exec span: model_kernel, device_id, gpu_memory_before_after, kvcache_miss_flag
- fallback span: origin (capacity/policy), fallback_latency_ms
- external-call span: e.g., KMS, DB for private deployments

Sampling strategy (practical):
- Base rate: 0.5% of all requests sampled for full traces (stratified by route and tenant size).
- Severity bump: on alert trigger (latency SLO breach or error-rate spike), increase to 10% for affected route and top 50 tenants for 30 minutes.
- Per-tenant cap: no tenant can account for > 30% of full-trace ingestion in an hour.
- Event-driven capture: allow ad-hoc capture for a specific request_id via console toggle for the duration of an investigation.

Investigation runway (step-by-step checklist):
1) Check Ring A panels: p99 latency, kvcache.hit.rate drops, batch size shifts, fallback rate spikes. If one of these correlates with incident window -> follow the specific play.
2) If Ring A unclear, escalate to Ring B: evaluate path mix and token-economics shifts (sudden seq length increases cause p99 jumps).
3) Trigger targeted trace capture (Ring C) for 5–20 request_ids sampled around the incident window.
4) If traces show host-level resource saturation -> correlate with infra telemetry and consider node drain/playbook.
5) If traces point to model-quality regressions (e.g., hallucination metric spikes in eval harness), open a model-rollout block and route traffic to previous variant.

Dashboard patterns and widgets (implementation notes):
- Top-left quick triage: single-row indicators (green/yellow/red) for p99 latency, error-rate, save cost burn rate. Clicking any indicator filters the rest of the dashboard to the incident window.
- Heatmap: tenant-by-hour incident heatmap for past 72h (color by p99 latency and token cost).
- Differential panel: week-over-week baseline compare for token-per-request and batch size (helps detect usage changes).
- Drilldown links: every row in metric table includes a link that opens a lightweight trace search with prefilled anchor tags.
- Compact incident card: when an alert fires, create a short-lived incident card with suggested next-hypothesis and one-click trace capture toggle.

Ownership matrix (suggested):
- Metric steward: who owns instrumentation for which metric (initial rotation):
  * queue_time, batch metrics -> eng-serving-runtime (Owen Li)
  * kvcache metrics -> applied-ml (Priya Nair)
  * model-selection & fallback -> platform-engineering (Sofia Martinez)
  * dashboard ownership and triage UX -> eng-observability (Maya Chen)

Cost-control knobs (hard limits + telemetry hygiene):
- Default retention: aggregated metrics 90d, detailed histograms 30d, full traces 7d (with archived-summaries)
- Trace budget: global budget (e.g., X GB/day) with soft alerts at 70% and hard stop at 100% unless manually escalated
- Query-cost meter: show estimated query cost on dashboards (approx. cost per dashboard refresh)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide exact numeric thresholds for adaptive sampling (discuss in weekly telemetry sync).
- Add an incident playbook template that pre-populates the investigation runway steps for oncall.
- Explore an automated experiment: if batch_size distribution shifts > 2 sigma and p99 latency rises, auto-increase sampling for that route.

Example short play (kv-cache drop):
- Symptom: kvcache.hit.rate drops from 98% -> 65% in 30m and p95 latency increases by 30%
- Quick checks: recent model rollout? prefix key schema change? cache eviction spikes on nodes?
- Action: pin previous model_variant for affected tenants, increase sampling for traces with kvcache_miss_flag, open infra ticket if host-level evictions present.

Notes-to-self / rough ideas (informal):
- Maybe add a "radar view" that auto-suggests next step (A/B/C) based on which ring shows deviation; simple decision tree first iteration.
- Keep the triage flow short: 5 checks that eliminate 80% of incidents.

Next steps / owners:
- Build initial dashboard prototype (Maya) by 2024-12-15
- Add sampling controls to Console (platform-engineering) - proposal by 2025-01-10
- Run pilot with two oncall rotations for 2 weeks and collect feedback (obs team)

References / links:
- JIRA:OBS-1234 (proposal for sampling controls)
- Confluence:OBS-INVESTIGATION-RUNWAY (draft playbook)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/456 (dashboard scaffold)

Unresolved decisions (write-up for sync):
- Fixed p99 latency threshold for major-alert vs minor-alert (sensitivity tradeoffs)
- Per-tenant trace caps: conservative vs generous approach and billing signal implications
- Automation threshold for auto-escalating sampling based on metric drift

End of doc.
